components.note: 亻 (person) — 俯 describes a person bending or looking downward.
府 (fǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 俯.

example.pinyin: Tā fǔshēn zài dìshàng zhǎo yàoshi.
example.english: He bent down and looked for the key on the ground.
example.fact: 俯 rarely appears alone — it's mostly seen in words like 俯视 (fǔshì, 'to look down from above') and 俯卧 (fǔwò, 'lying face down').

components.note: 厂 (a simple shelter or workshop) — the semantic link is loose here; 厘 mainly serves as a measure word for a tiny unit.
里 (lǐ) gives a sound close to lí, sharing the rhyme but differing in tone.

example.pinyin: Yì límǐ fēicháng duǎn.
example.english: One centimeter is very short.
example.fact: 厘 shows up in 厘米 (límǐ, 'centimeter'), the everyday measurement word built from this character.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 愣 describes a mental state, being caught off guard or dazed.
罒, stacked with 方 to form the right side, gives a sound only loosely related to lèng today — the phonetic link has drifted noticeably over time.

example.pinyin: Tā tīngdào xiāoxi, lèng zhù le.
example.english: He was stunned when he heard the news.
example.fact: 愣住 (lèngzhù) is the common way to say 'to be stunned, taken aback' — 愣 rarely stands alone.

meanings: abbr. for Xiamen or Amoy 廈門|厦门[Xia4 men2], Fujian

components.note: 厂 (a simple shelter or building outline) — 厦 refers to a large building or mansion.
夏 (xià) gives a sound close to shà, sharing the rhyme but differing in the initial consonant.

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò dàshà yǒu wǔshí céng.
example.english: This building has fifty floors.
example.fact: 厦 usually appears in 大厦 (dàshà, 'large building, tower'), the word used for skyscrapers and office towers.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恳 describes a sincere, heartfelt attitude.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound close to kěn, sharing the rhyme and a related initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 他恳求老师再给他一次机会。
example.pinyin: Tā kěnqiú lǎoshī zài gěi tā yí cì jīhuì.
example.english: He earnestly begged the teacher to give him one more chance.
example.fact: 恳 often appears in 恳求 (kěnqiú, 'to earnestly beg') and 诚恳 (chéngkěn, 'sincere'), always carrying a tone of sincerity.

components.note: 饣 (food) — 饶 was originally tied to abundance of food, later broadening to mean plentiful in general.
尧 (yáo) gives a sound close to ráo, sharing the rhyme -áo.

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī ráo le tā zhè yí cì.
example.english: The teacher let him off this time.
example.fact: 饶 often appears in 饶了 (ráo le, 'to let someone off, forgive'), a common phrase for showing mercy.

meanings: to keep at sb (to do sth)
etymologyHint: A metal 钅 nail 丁; 丁 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 钅 (metal) shows what the nail is made of.
丁 depicts the simple shape of a nail or peg.

example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng yǒu yí gè dīngzi.
example.english: There's a nail on the wall.
example.fact: 钉 is almost always used as 钉子 (dīngzi, 'nail'), the small metal item used to hang things.

example.pinyin: Tā shì guǎfù, yí gè rén shēnghuó.
example.english: She is a widow and lives alone.
example.fact: 寡 appears almost exclusively in 寡妇 (guǎfù, 'widow'), a fixed word for a woman whose husband has died.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 憾 describes an emotional sense of regret or dissatisfaction.
感 (gǎn) gives a sound close to hàn, sharing the rhyme -an.

example.hanzi: 他没能参加比赛,感到很遗憾。
example.pinyin: Tā méi néng cānjiā bǐsài, gǎndào hěn yíhàn.
example.english: He couldn't take part in the competition and felt very regretful.
example.fact: 憾 almost always appears in 遗憾 (yíhàn, 'regret, pity'), rarely standing alone.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 摔 involves a hand-related action of throwing down or a body falling.
率 (shuài) gives a sound close to shuāi, sharing the same initial and a similar rhyme.

example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, bié shuāidǎo le!
example.english: Be careful, don't fall down!
example.fact: 摔 combines with 倒 to form 摔倒 (shuāidǎo, 'to fall down'), a common phrase parents say to children.

etymologyHint: Clothes 叒 stacked on top of a drawer 冝

components.note: 叒 depicts layers stacked one on another, like folded clothes.
冝 suggests a container or drawer beneath the pile — together giving 叠 its meaning 'to stack, fold up.'

example.hanzi: 把衣服叠好放进箱子里。
example.pinyin: Bǎ yīfu dié hǎo fàng jìn xiāngzi lǐ.
example.english: Fold the clothes and put them in the box.
example.fact: 叠 is the character used for folding clothes (叠衣服, dié yīfu) and for stacking things up.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 惹 describes provoking an emotional reaction in someone.
若 (ruò) gives a sound distantly related to rě, sharing the initial r- but the rhyme has drifted over time.

example.pinyin: Bié rě tā shēngqì.
example.english: Don't make her angry.
example.fact: 惹 is common in 惹...生气 (to make someone angry) and 惹麻烦 (rě máfan, 'to cause trouble').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 喻 relates to explaining something through speech.
俞 (yú) gives a sound close to yù, sharing the same rhyme and a related tone.

example.hanzi: 老师用比喻讲解这个词。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī yòng bǐyù jiǎngjiě zhège cí.
example.english: The teacher used a metaphor to explain this word.
example.fact: 喻 often appears in 比喻 (bǐyù, 'metaphor, analogy'), a word used often in Chinese classrooms.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谱 relates to a written or spoken record, like a chart or score.
普 (pǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 谱.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì shǒu gē de yuèpǔ.
example.english: This is the sheet music for a song.
example.fact: 谱 appears in 乐谱 (yuèpǔ, 'musical score') and 食谱 (shípǔ, 'recipe'), both meaning an organized chart or list.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 愧 describes an emotional state of shame or guilt.
鬼 (guǐ) gives a sound close to kuì, sharing the initial and a similar rhyme.

example.hanzi: 他做错了事,感到很愧疚。
example.pinyin: Tā zuò cuò le shì, gǎndào hěn kuìjiù.
example.english: He did something wrong and felt very guilty.
example.fact: 愧 usually appears in 愧疚 (kuìjiù) and 惭愧 (cánkuì), both meaning a feeling of guilt or shame.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 煌 describes brightness, like the glow of fire.
皇 (huáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 煌.

example.hanzi: 敦煌有很多古老的壁画。
example.pinyin: Dūnhuáng yǒu hěn duō gǔlǎo de bìhuà.
example.english: Dunhuang has many ancient murals.
example.fact: 煌 almost always appears in 敦煌 (Dūnhuáng), a famous city on the old Silk Road known for its cave art, or in 辉煌 (huīhuáng, 'brilliant, glorious').

example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen xuéxiào de xiàohuī.
example.english: This is our school's badge.
example.fact: 徽 usually appears in 校徽 (xiàohuī, 'school badge') and 国徽 (guóhuī, 'national emblem'), and is also short for Anhui province (安徽, Ānhuī).

components.note: 氵 (water) — 溶 describes a substance dissolving in liquid.
容 (róng) gives the sound — an exact match with 溶.

example.pinyin: Táng zài shuǐ lǐ rónghuà le.
example.english: The sugar dissolved in the water.
example.fact: 溶 appears in 溶化 (rónghuà) and 溶解 (róngjiě), both meaning 'to dissolve.'

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坠 describes something falling down toward the ground.
队 (duì) gives a sound distantly related to zhuì, sharing the rhyme -uì but the initial consonant has drifted over time.

example.pinyin: Píngguǒ cóng shù shàng zhuìluò xiàlái.
example.english: The apple fell down from the tree.
example.fact: 坠 often appears in 坠落 (zhuìluò, 'to fall, plummet'), describing something dropping from a height.

example.pinyin: Tā tūrán shāchē, chē tíng le.
example.english: He suddenly braked, and the car stopped.
example.fact: 煞 appears in 煞车 (shāchē), an alternate way to write 刹车 ('to brake'), a word every driver needs.

etymologyHint: A curtain or towel hanging from a rack

components.note: 巾 depicts a piece of cloth draped over a rod — its simple vertical lines mirror a hanging towel or curtain.

example.pinyin: Tā yòng máojīn cā shǒu.
example.english: He wiped his hands with a towel.
example.fact: 巾 rarely stands alone — it commonly appears in 毛巾 (máojīn, 'towel') and 围巾 (wéijīn, 'scarf').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 滥 describes water overflowing, extended to mean excess in general.
监 (jiān) gives a sound only distantly related to làn today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Búyào lànyòng yàowù.
example.english: Don't misuse medicine.
example.fact: 滥 often appears in 滥用 (lànyòng, 'to abuse, misuse'), a common word about overusing something harmful.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 洒 describes scattering or spilling liquid.
西 (xī) gives a sound only distantly related to sǎ today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ shuǐ sǎ dào le dìshàng.
example.english: He spilled water onto the floor.
example.fact: 洒 describes scattering or spilling liquid, as in 洒水 (sǎshuǐ, 'to sprinkle water').

meanings: to block up (a road, pipe etc)

components.note: 土 (earth) — 堵 relates to blocking something, like a wall of earth.
者 (zhě) gives a sound only distantly related to dǔ today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Lù shàng dǔchē le.
example.english: The road is jammed with traffic.
example.fact: 堵 is the character in 堵车 (dǔchē, 'traffic jam'), one of the most commonly heard phrases in Chinese cities.

components.note: 瓦 (tile, pottery) — 瓷 refers to a fired clay material, porcelain.
次 (cì) gives a sound close to cí, sharing the same rhyme with a shifted tone.

example.pinyin: Zhège wǎn shì cí zuò de.
example.english: This bowl is made of porcelain.
example.fact: 瓷 appears in 瓷器 (cíqì, 'porcelain, chinaware'), a craft China has been famous for since ancient times.

example.hanzi: 电影里,巫师念了一句咒语。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ, wūshī niàn le yí jù zhòuyǔ.
example.english: In the movie, the wizard recited a spell.
example.fact: 咒 usually appears in 咒语 (zhòuyǔ, 'magic spell') and 咒骂 (zhòumà, 'to curse at someone').

components.note: 女 (woman) — 姨 names a female relative.
夷 (yí) gives the sound — an exact match with 姨.

example.pinyin: Wǒ āyí shì lǎoshī.
example.english: My aunt is a teacher.
example.fact: 姨 appears in 阿姨 (āyí), used both for 'maternal aunt' and, more broadly, as a polite way to address an older woman.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 棒 describes an object made of wood, a stick.
奉 (fèng) gives a sound only distantly related to bàng today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā de Hànyǔ shuō de hěn bàng.
example.english: His Chinese is spoken very well.
example.fact: 棒 originally means 'stick, club,' but in everyday speech it's mostly used as an adjective meaning 'great, awesome.'

components.note: 阝 (on the right, from 邑 'settlement') — 郡 was an old administrative region, a type of place.
君 (jūn) gives a sound close to jùn, sharing the same rhyme and a related tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì gǔdài de yí gè jùn.
example.english: This was an ancient administrative region.
example.fact: 郡 was a unit of local government in ancient China, similar to a county or prefecture — today it mostly appears in historical contexts and place names.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 浴 relates to washing with water.
谷 (gǔ) gives a sound only distantly related to yù today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Yùshì lǐ yǒu rè shuǐ.
example.english: There is hot water in the bathroom.
example.fact: 浴 appears in 浴室 (yùshì, 'bathroom') and 洗浴 (xǐyù, 'to bathe'), always related to washing.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 媚 originally described a woman's charm.
眉 (méi) gives a sound close to mèi, sharing the same rhyme with a shifted tone.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān yángguāng míngmèi.
example.english: Today the sunshine is bright and beautiful.
example.fact: 媚 often appears in 明媚 (míngmèi, 'bright and beautiful'), a common word to describe sunny weather or pretty scenery.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 稣 was originally tied to reviving or gathering grain.
鱼 (yú) gives a sound only distantly related to sū today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 耶稣是基督教的重要人物。
example.pinyin: Yēsū shì Jīdūjiào de zhòngyào rénwù.
example.english: Jesus is an important figure in Christianity.
example.fact: 稣 today is used almost only in 耶稣 (Yēsū, 'Jesus'), a phonetic transliteration with little connection to its original grain-related meaning.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 淮 names a river.
隹 (zhuī) gives a sound only distantly related to huái today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 淮河是中国的一条大河。
example.pinyin: Huáihé shì Zhōngguó de yì tiáo dà hé.
example.english: The Huai River is a major river in China.
example.fact: 淮 is used almost exclusively in the name 淮河 (Huáihé, the Huai River), one of China's principal rivers.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哎 is a sound made with the mouth, an interjection.
艾 (ài) gives a sound close to āi, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Āi, wǒ wàng dài yàoshi le!
example.english: Oh no, I forgot to bring my keys!
example.fact: 哎 is an interjection used to express surprise or mild frustration, much like 'oh' in English.

components.note: 尸 (body) — 屁 relates to a bodily function.
比 (bǐ) gives a sound only distantly related to pì today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu fàng le yí gè pì.
example.english: The puppy let out a fart.
example.fact: 屁 is an everyday, casual word — it appears in 放屁 (fàngpì, 'to fart') and, informally, in 屁话 (pìhuà, 'nonsense talk').

etymologyHint: The sap 氵 of the varnish tree 桼; 桼 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 氵 (water) suggests a liquid substance.
桼 depicts the varnish tree from which lacquer sap is drawn — combined with water, it shows the fluid taken from the tree.

example.pinyin: Zhè bǎ yǐzi shuā le xīn qī.
example.english: This chair was painted with new lacquer.
example.fact: 漆 refers to paint or lacquer, as in 油漆 (yóuqī, 'paint'), a coating brushed onto surfaces like wood or metal.

example.pinyin: Yínyǔ lián xià le hǎo jǐ tiān.
example.english: The prolonged rain kept falling for several days.
example.fact: 淫 originally meant 'excessive' — 淫雨 (yínyǔ) is an old literary term for days of unrelenting rain; the character's modern meaning developed later.

etymologyHint: A nest 巛田 built in a tree 木

components.note: 巛 depicts twisted twigs or straw, evoking the woven strands of a nest.
木 (tree) shows where the nest is built.

example.hanzi: 那只鸟在树上做了一个巢。
example.pinyin: Nà zhī niǎo zài shù shàng zuò le yí gè cháo.
example.english: That bird built a nest in the tree.
example.fact: 巢 means 'nest' and often appears in 鸟巢 (niǎocháo, 'bird's nest'), also the nickname for Beijing's Olympic stadium.

meanings: used in transliteration of chemical compounds

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 吩 relates to speaking, giving an instruction.
分 (fēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 吩.

example.pinyin: Māma fēnfù wǒ dǎsǎo fángjiān.
example.english: Mom told me to clean the room.
example.fact: 吩 almost always appears in 吩咐 (fēnfù, 'to instruct, tell someone to do something').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 撰 relates to composing or putting together in writing (originally a hand-related action).
巽 (xùn) gives a sound only distantly related to zhuàn today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài zhuànxiě yì běn shū.
example.english: He is writing a book.
example.fact: 撰 is a formal word for writing, as in 撰写 (zhuànxiě, 'to compose, write') — used for books and articles, not everyday notes.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 啸 describes a loud sound made with the mouth, a howl or roar.
肃 (sù) gives a sound only distantly related to xiào today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Fēng zài chuāng wài hūxiào.
example.english: The wind howled outside the window.
example.fact: 啸 often appears in 呼啸 (hūxiào, 'to howl, whistle'), describing the sound of strong wind.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 滞 originally described water that wouldn't flow, extended to mean stagnant in general.
带 (dài) gives a sound only distantly related to zhì today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Gōngzuò jìnzhǎn tíngzhì le.
example.english: The work's progress has stalled.
example.fact: 滞 usually appears in 停滞 (tíngzhì, 'to stagnate, come to a standstill').

components.note: 王 (jade, written as 王 in components) — 玫 originally described a type of fine jade or gem.
攵 gives a sound only distantly related to méi today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā sòng le tā yì duǒ méiguī.
example.english: He gave her a rose.
example.fact: 玫 appears almost exclusively in 玫瑰 (méiguī, 'rose'), the flower name.

etymologyHint: Like a sheet 页 of stone 石

components.note: 页 depicts a flat sheet, suggesting something broad.
石 (stone) shows solidity and size, contributing to 硕's meaning 'large, great.'

example.pinyin: Tā huòdé le shuòshì xuéwèi.
example.english: He obtained a master's degree.
example.fact: 硕 today is mostly seen in 硕士 (shuòshì, 'master's degree'), a title held by many graduate students.

meanings: to fish with a hook and line; to angle
etymologyHint: A metal 钅 hook 勺; 勺 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 钅 (metal) shows the material of the fishing hook.
勺 depicts a small curved shape, echoed in the curve of a fishing hook.

example.pinyin: Bàba xǐhuan qù hébiān diàoyú.
example.english: Dad likes to go fishing by the river.
example.fact: 钓 is almost always used in 钓鱼 (diàoyú, 'to fish'), a common leisure activity.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蝶 names an insect, the butterfly.
枼 (yè) gives a sound only distantly related to dié today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō húdié.
example.english: There are many butterflies in the park.
example.fact: 蝶 almost always appears in 蝴蝶 (húdié, 'butterfly'), rarely standing alone.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 膝 names a body part, the knee.
桼 (qī) gives a sound only distantly related to xī today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā guì zài dìshàng, xīgài téng.
example.english: He knelt on the ground, and his knee hurt.
example.fact: 膝 almost always appears in 膝盖 (xīgài, 'knee'), the body part word.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 姚 was originally used to describe a graceful appearance.
兆 (zhào) gives a sound only distantly related to yáo today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 姚明是一位著名的篮球运动员。
example.pinyin: Yáo Míng shì yí wèi zhùmíng de lánqiú yùndòngyuán.
example.english: Yao Ming is a famous basketball player.
example.fact: 姚 is mainly used as a surname, as in the basketball star 姚明 (Yáo Míng).

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 茂 describes plants growing thick and lush.
戊 (wù) gives a sound only distantly related to mào today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shān shàng de shùmù hěn màoshèng.
example.english: The trees on the mountain are lush and thriving.
example.fact: 茂 usually appears in 茂盛 (màoshèng, 'lush, flourishing'), describing plants growing thickly.

components.note: 身 (body) — 躯 refers to the human body.
区 (qū) gives the sound — an exact match with 躯.

example.pinyin: Tā de shēnqū hěn qiángzhuàng.
example.english: His body is very strong.
example.fact: 躯 is a formal word for 'body,' as in 身躯 (shēnqū) — everyday speech usually uses 身体 (shēntǐ) instead.

example.hanzi: 古代的官吏要为百姓做事。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài de guānlì yào wèi bǎixìng zuò shì.
example.english: Ancient officials had to work for the common people.
example.fact: 吏 is an old word for a government official — it survives today mainly in 官吏 (guānlì, 'officials') and historical contexts.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 猿 names an animal, the ape.
袁 (yuán) gives the sound — an exact match with 猿.

example.pinyin: Yuán shì yì zhǒng cōngmíng de dòngwù.
example.english: Apes are a kind of intelligent animal.
example.fact: 猿 means 'ape' and appears in words like 猿人 (yuánrén, 'ape-man'), referring to early human ancestors.

etymologyHint: A fortress 宀 with walls made of wood 木

components.note: 宀 (roof/shelter) shows an enclosed structure, like a fortress.
木 (wood) shows the material of the fortress's walls.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè gǔlǎo de shānzhài.
example.english: This is an old mountain stockade.
example.fact: 寨 usually appears in 山寨 (shānzhài, 'mountain stronghold'), which today also colloquially means 'knockoff, counterfeit.'

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恕 describes a heartfelt willingness to forgive.
如 (rú) gives a sound only distantly related to shù today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā qǐngqiú péngyou de kuānshù.
example.english: He asked his friend for forgiveness.
example.fact: 恕 usually appears in 宽恕 (kuānshù, 'to forgive') and the polite phrase 恕我 (shù wǒ, 'pardon me, excuse me').

etymologyHint: A ditch 洰 made of wood 木; 洰 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 洰 combines water with another element, suggesting a channel that carries water.
木 (wood) may reflect wooden supports lining the ditch.

example.pinyin: Nóngmín wā le yì tiáo shuǐqú.
example.english: The farmer dug an irrigation ditch.
example.fact: 渠 usually appears in 水渠 (shuǐqú, 'irrigation channel, ditch').

etymologyHint: A younger brother 尗 killed in a war 戈

components.note: 尗 depicts a young person, a younger family member.
戈 (an ancient dagger-axe) points to a connection with conflict — together the parts trace back to a relative's hardship in war, which is how 戚 came to mean both 'relative' and 'sad.'

example.pinyin: Wǒmen shì qīnqi.
example.english: We are relatives.
example.fact: 戚 today mainly appears in 亲戚 (qīnqi, 'relative'), one of the first family words learners encounter.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān shì tā de shēngchén.
example.english: Today is his birthday.
example.fact: 辰 appears in 生辰 (shēngchén, a formal word for 'birthday') and 时辰 (shíchen, an old unit of time equal to two hours).

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 舶 names a type of large vessel, a ship.
白 (bái) gives a sound only distantly related to bó today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Gǎngkǒu tíngzhe hěn duō chuánbó.
example.english: Many ships are docked at the harbor.
example.fact: 舶 usually appears in 船舶 (chuánbó, 'ships, vessels'), a formal collective word for boats.

etymologyHint: To pass out 分 a booklet 页; 分 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 分 (to divide, distribute) shows the act of handing something out.
页 (a page or document) suggests a certificate or notice being given out.

example.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng gěi xuésheng bānfā jiǎngzhuàng.
example.english: The principal awarded certificates to the students.
example.fact: 颁 usually appears in 颁发 (bānfā, 'to award, issue'), for ceremonies giving out prizes or certificates.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 惶 describes an emotional state of fear or anxiety.
皇 (huáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 惶.

example.pinyin: Tā huángkǒng de kànzhe lǎoshī.
example.english: He looked at the teacher in a frightened panic.
example.fact: 惶 usually appears in 惶恐 (huángkǒng, 'terrified, apprehensive') and 惊惶 (jīnghuáng, 'panicked').

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 狐 names an animal, the fox.
瓜 (guā) gives a sound only distantly related to hú today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ yǒu yì zhī húli.
example.english: There is a fox in the forest.
example.fact: 狐 almost always appears in 狐狸 (húli, 'fox'), rarely standing alone.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讽 relates to speaking, in this case mocking through words.
风 (fēng) gives a sound close to fěng, sharing the same initial and rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他说的话带着讽刺的意味。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō de huà dàizhe fěngcì de yìwèi.
example.english: What he said carried a sarcastic tone.
example.fact: 讽 usually appears in 讽刺 (fěngcì, 'to satirize, mock').

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 笨 originally related to the plain, unworked core of bamboo, later extending to mean dull or clumsy.
本 (běn) gives a sound close to bèn, sharing the same rhyme with a shifted tone.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān hěn bèn, wàng le dài shū.
example.english: I was silly today — I forgot to bring my book.
example.fact: 笨 is the common word for 'stupid, clumsy,' as in 笨蛋 (bèndàn, 'idiot,' used jokingly among friends).

etymologyHint: A cloth 衤 wrap 包; 包 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 衤 (clothing) shows this is a garment.
包 (to wrap) suggests a garment that wraps around the body, like a robe.

example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yí jiàn cháng páo.
example.english: He is wearing a long robe.
example.fact: 袍 refers to a long robe or gown, as in 旗袍 (qípáo), the traditional fitted Chinese dress.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嘲 relates to speaking, in this case mocking someone.
朝 (cháo) gives the sound — an exact match with 嘲.

example.pinyin: Bié cháoxiào biéren.
example.english: Don't laugh at other people.
example.fact: 嘲 usually appears in 嘲笑 (cháoxiào, 'to mock, ridicule').

meanings: (used in loanwords for its phonetic value)

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 啡 is used in a word for something taken by mouth (coffee).
非 (fēi) gives the sound — an exact match with 啡.

example.hanzi: 我每天早上喝一杯咖啡。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang hē yì bēi kāfēi.
example.english: I drink a cup of coffee every morning.
example.fact: 啡 only appears in 咖啡 (kāfēi, 'coffee'), a word borrowed phonetically from a foreign language.

etymologyHint: To send forth 发 water 氵

components.note: 发 (to send out, release) shows the action of casting something forth.
氵 (water) specifies what is being cast — splashing water.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ shuǐ pō dào le huāyuán lǐ.
example.english: She splashed water into the garden.
example.fact: 泼 describes splashing or throwing liquid, as in 泼水 (pōshuǐ, 'to splash water'), central to the Water-Splashing Festival celebrated by the Dai ethnic group.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 衔 originally referred to a metal bit held in a horse's mouth.
行 (xíng) gives a sound close to xián, sharing the initial with a rhyme that has drifted over time.

example.pinyin: Gǒu zuǐ lǐ xiánzhe yì gēn gútou.
example.english: The dog is holding a bone in its mouth.
example.fact: 衔 means 'to hold in the mouth,' as in 衔着 (xiánzhe), often describing animals carrying things.

etymologyHint: A curled-up 卷 person 亻; 卷 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 亻 (person) shows this describes a person's state.
卷 depicts something curled or rolled up, like a tired person curling up to rest.

example.hanzi: 他工作了一天,感到很疲倦。
example.pinyin: Tā gōngzuò le yì tiān, gǎndào hěn píjuàn.
example.english: He worked all day and felt very tired.
example.fact: 倦 usually appears in 疲倦 (píjuàn, 'weary, tired').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 涵 relates to soaking or holding, like water contained within something.
函 (hán) gives the sound — an exact match with 涵.

example.hanzi: 这句话涵盖了很多意思。
example.pinyin: Zhè jù huà hángài le hěn duō yìsi.
example.english: This sentence covers many meanings.
example.fact: 涵 usually appears in 涵盖 (hángài, 'to cover, encompass') and 内涵 (nèihán, 'connotation, inner meaning').

etymologyHint: A small 小 bird 隹

components.note: 小 (small) shows the bird's small size.
隹 (a short-tailed bird) forms the base image, together giving 雀 its meaning 'small bird, sparrow.'

example.pinyin: Shù shàng yǒu yì zhī xiǎo máquè.
example.english: There's a little sparrow in the tree.
example.fact: 雀 usually appears in 麻雀 (máquè, 'sparrow'), one of the most common birds in China.

etymologyHint: A cycle 勹 of ten days 日; a traditional week

components.note: 勹 (a wrapping, enclosing shape) suggests a bounded cycle.
日 (sun/day) shows this unit is made of days — specifically a span of ten.

example.hanzi: 这个月上旬他去了北京。
example.pinyin: Zhège yuè shàngxún tā qùle Běijīng.
example.english: In the first ten days of this month, he went to Beijing.
example.fact: 旬 divides a month into three ten-day periods: 上旬 (early), 中旬 (mid), and 下旬 (late).

components.note: 亻 (person) — 僵 describes a person's body becoming stiff.
畺 (jiāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 僵.

example.hanzi: 天气太冷,他的手冻僵了。
example.pinyin: Tiānqì tài lěng, tā de shǒu dòngjiāng le.
example.english: The weather is too cold, and his hands froze stiff.
example.fact: 僵 usually appears in 僵硬 (jiāngyìng, 'stiff, rigid') and 冻僵 (dòngjiāng, 'frozen stiff').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 撕 describes a hand-related action, tearing something apart.
斯 (sī) gives the sound — an exact match with 撕.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhǐ sī chéng le liǎng bàn.
example.english: He tore the paper into two halves.
example.fact: 撕 means 'to tear, rip,' as in 撕纸 (sī zhǐ, 'to tear paper').

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 肢 names body parts, the limbs.
支 (zhī) gives the sound — an exact match with 肢.

example.pinyin: Rén yǒu sìzhī.
example.english: People have four limbs.
example.fact: 肢 usually appears in 四肢 (sìzhī, 'the four limbs') and 肢体 (zhītǐ, 'limbs, body').

meanings: crop row; mounded soil forming a ridge in a field

components.note: 土 (earth) — 垄 describes a raised ridge of earth in a field.
龙 (lóng) gives a sound close to lǒng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 农民在田里种了一垄玉米。
example.pinyin: Nóngmín zài tián lǐ zhòng le yì lǒng yùmǐ.
example.english: The farmer planted a row of corn in the field.
example.fact: 垄 usually describes a raised ridge in a field, as in 垄断 (lǒngduàn, 'to monopolize'), which originally referred to controlling the high ground of a market.

meanings: non-Han people, esp. to the East of China
etymologyHint: A man 大 armed with a bow 弓

components.note: 大 depicts a person, seen from the front with arms and legs spread.
弓 (a bow) shows the person carrying a weapon — together an early image of an armed outsider.

example.hanzi: 他化险为夷,平安回家了。
example.pinyin: Tā huàxiǎn wéiyí, píng'ān huí jiā le.
example.english: He turned danger into safety and got home safely.
example.fact: 夷 survives today mainly in the idiom 化险为夷 (huàxiǎn wéiyí, 'to turn danger into safety'); historically it was also used to refer to peoples outside Chinese culture.

meanings: (bound form) to surpass the ordinary; outstanding
etymologyHint: To run 辶 like a rabbit 兔

components.note: 辶 (to walk, move) shows motion.
兔 (rabbit) suggests swift, fleeing movement — together giving 逸 its meaning 'to escape, flee.'

example.pinyin: Tā chènjī táoyì le.
example.english: He seized the chance and fled.
example.fact: 逸 usually appears in 逃逸 (táoyì, 'to flee, escape') and 安逸 (ānyì, 'comfortable, carefree').

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 茅 names a type of plant, a reed or rush.
矛 (máo) gives the sound — an exact match with 茅.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì jiān máowū.
example.english: This is a thatched hut.
example.fact: 茅 means a kind of reed or grass, as in 茅屋 (máowū, 'thatched cottage').

components.note: 亻 (person) — 侨 describes a person living away from home.
乔 (qiáo) gives the sound — an exact match with 侨.

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi huáqiáo.
example.english: He is an overseas Chinese person.
example.fact: 侨 usually appears in 华侨 (huáqiáo, 'overseas Chinese') and 侨民 (qiáomín, 'expatriate').

etymologyHint: A cart 车 carried on one's shoulder 舁

components.note: 车 (cart) is the object being carried.
舁 depicts pairs of hands lifting together — combined with the cart, an image of carrying a palanquin, which extended to 舆's broader sense of 'shared, public.'

example.hanzi: 这件事引起了很多舆论。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yǐnqǐ le hěn duō yúlùn.
example.english: This matter stirred up a lot of public opinion.
example.fact: 舆 usually appears in 舆论 (yúlùn, 'public opinion'), a word often seen in news and media.

etymologyHint: An oven 穴 where pots 缶 are fired; 缶 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 穴 (a cave or hole) shows an enclosed space like a kiln.
缶 (an earthen jar) shows the pottery being fired inside.

example.hanzi: 这些碗是在窑里烧出来的。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē wǎn shì zài yáo lǐ shāo chūlái de.
example.english: These bowls were fired in a kiln.
example.fact: 窑 usually appears in 窑洞 (yáodòng, a cave dwelling common in northern China) and 陶瓷窑 (a pottery kiln).

meanings: (literary) alunite (formerly used as a black dye)

components.note: 氵 (water) — 涅 was originally tied to dark, wet mud used as a dye.
圼 gives a sound close to niè, sharing a related rhyme.

example.pinyin: Fójiào zhōng yǒu nièpán de gàiniàn.
example.english: In Buddhism, there is the concept of nirvana.
example.fact: 涅 today appears almost only in 涅槃 (nièpán, 'nirvana'), a Buddhist term transliterated from Sanskrit.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 蒲 names a type of water plant, a rush.
浦 (pǔ) gives a sound close to pú, sharing the same rhyme with a shifted tone.

example.pinyin: Hú biān zhǎngzhe hěn duō púcǎo.
example.english: Many rushes grow by the lake.
example.fact: 蒲 refers to a type of reed or rush that grows near water, as in 菖蒲 (chāngpú, 'calamus') and the surname 蒲 (Pú).

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谦 describes how one speaks or presents oneself, modestly.
兼 (jiān) gives a sound close to qiān, sharing the same rhyme with a different initial.

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè hěn qiānxū de rén.
example.english: He is a very modest person.
example.fact: 谦 usually appears in 谦虚 (qiānxū, 'modest, humble'), a quality highly valued in Chinese culture.

meanings: abbr. for Hangzhou 杭州[Hang2 zhou1]

components.note: 木 (wood) — 杭 was originally tied to a wooden vessel used to cross water.
亢 (kàng) gives a sound only distantly related to háng today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 杭州是一个很美的城市。
example.pinyin: Hángzhōu shì yí gè hěn měi de chéngshì.
example.english: Hangzhou is a very beautiful city.
example.fact: 杭 is mainly used in 杭州 (Hángzhōu), a famous city known for its West Lake.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 噢 is a sound made with the mouth, an interjection.
奥 (ào) gives a sound only distantly related to ō today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Ō, wǒ míngbai le!
example.english: Oh, I understand now!
example.fact: 噢 is an interjection used to show sudden realization, similar to 'oh' in English.

etymologyHint: Two hands 廾 breaking something 敝; 敝 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 廾 depicts two hands.
敝 shows something worn out or broken — together suggesting hands causing damage, which is how 弊 came to mean 'harm, malpractice.'

example.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò yǒu hěn duō bìduān.
example.english: Doing it this way has many drawbacks.
example.fact: 弊 usually appears in 弊端 (bìduān, 'malpractice, drawback') and 舞弊 (wǔbì, 'to cheat, engage in fraud').

components.note: 力 (strength) — 勋 relates to achievement earned through effort.
员 (yuán) gives a sound only distantly related to xūn today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā wèi guójiā lìxià le gōngxūn.
example.english: He achieved great merit for his country.
example.fact: 勋 usually appears in 功勋 (gōngxūn, 'meritorious service') and 勋章 (xūnzhāng, 'medal').

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刮 describes a scraping action done with a blade.
舌 (shé) gives a sound only distantly related to guā today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn zài guā dàfēng.
example.english: There's a strong wind blowing outside.
example.fact: 刮 describes scraping or a strong wind blowing, as in 刮风 (guāfēng, 'the wind is blowing').

components.note: 阝 (place) — 郊 refers to an area outside a city, a type of place.
交 (jiāo) gives the sound — an exact match with 郊.

example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù jiāowài yěcān.
example.english: This weekend we're going to the outskirts for a picnic.
example.fact: 郊 usually appears in 郊区 (jiāoqū, 'suburbs') and 郊外 (jiāowài, 'outskirts, countryside').

components.note: 冫 (ice) — 凄 describes a cold, bleak feeling.
妻 (qī) gives the sound — an exact match with 凄.

example.pinyin: Diànyǐng de jiéjú hěn qīliáng.
example.english: The movie's ending was very bleak and sad.
example.fact: 凄 usually appears in 凄凉 (qīliáng, 'desolate, bleak') and 凄惨 (qīcǎn, 'miserable').

meanings: to hold or offer with both hands
classifier for what can be held in both hands
etymologyHint: An offering 奉 made with two hands 扌; 奉 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows this action is done with the hands.
奉 depicts something being offered up respectfully — together with the hand radical, giving 捧's meaning 'to hold up with both hands.'

example.pinyin: Tā shuāngshǒu pěngzhe yì běn shū.
example.english: She held a book up with both hands.
example.fact: 捧 describes holding something carefully with both hands, and also appears in 捧场 (pěngchǎng, 'to support, cheer someone on').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 浸 describes soaking something in liquid.
彐, part of the character's right side, gives a sound only distantly related to jìn today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ máojīn jìn zài shuǐ lǐ.
example.english: He soaked the towel in water.
example.fact: 浸 means 'to soak, immerse,' as in 浸泡 (jìnpào, 'to soak').

components.note: 石 (stone) — 砖 names a material made from fired earth, a brick.
专 (zhuān) gives the sound — an exact match with 砖.

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò fángzi shì yòng zhuān jiàn de.
example.english: This house is built with bricks.
example.fact: 砖 means 'brick,' as in 砖头 (zhuāntou, 'a brick').

meanings: to enter upon a period of (classical)
one of the 64 hexagrams of the Book of Changes
etymologyHint: A cauldron on its bronze tripod

components.note: 鼎 depicts an ancient bronze cauldron standing on three legs with two handles on top, a vessel used in ceremonies.

example.hanzi: 博物馆里有一个古代的鼎。
example.pinyin: Bówùguǎn lǐ yǒu yí gè gǔdài de dǐng.
example.english: There is an ancient bronze cauldron in the museum.
example.fact: 鼎 was an ancient ritual vessel and today appears in idioms like 一言九鼎 (yì yán jiǔ dǐng, 'one's word carries great weight').

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 篮 names an object often woven from bamboo, a basket.
监 (jiān) gives a sound only distantly related to lán today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 她拿着一个篮子去买菜。
example.pinyin: Tā ná zhe yí gè lánzi qù mǎi cài.
example.english: She carried a basket to buy groceries.
example.fact: 篮 usually appears in 篮子 (lánzi, 'basket') and 篮球 (lánqiú, 'basketball').

meanings: torch made from hemp stalks or bamboo (old)
etymologyHint: Steam 烝 provides the meaning and sound

components.note: 艹 sits atop the character but contributes little independent meaning here; the imagery mostly comes from the part below.
烝 depicts heat and something rising above a fire, an image of vapor rising — giving 蒸 its meaning 'to steam.'

example.pinyin: Māma zài zhēng bāozi.
example.english: Mom is steaming buns.
example.fact: 蒸 describes cooking with steam, as in 蒸包子 (zhēng bāozi, 'to steam buns') and 蒸饭 (zhēngfàn, 'to steam rice').

components.note: 饣 (food) — 饼 names a type of food, a flat cake.
并 (bìng) gives a sound close to bǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī yuèbǐng.
example.english: I like eating mooncakes.
example.fact: 饼 refers to flat, round cakes or breads, as in 月饼 (yuèbǐng, 'mooncake') and 饼干 (bǐnggān, 'cookie, cracker').

meanings: mu, Chinese unit of area equal to 1

components.note: 田 (field) — 亩 is a traditional unit for measuring farmland.

example.pinyin: Zhè kuài dì yǒu shí mǔ.
example.english: This piece of land is ten mu (a Chinese unit of area).
example.fact: 亩 is a traditional Chinese unit of land area, still used today especially in agriculture — one mu is about 667 square meters.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 肾 refers to an internal organ, the kidney.

example.pinyin: Shèn shì réntǐ zhòngyào de qìguān.
example.english: The kidney is an important organ in the human body.
example.fact: 肾 means 'kidney,' one of the vital organs that filters the blood.

components.note: 阝 (hill) — 陡 describes a steep incline.
走 (zǒu) gives a sound only distantly related to dǒu today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo shānlù hěn dǒu.
example.english: This mountain road is very steep.
example.fact: 陡 describes something steep, as in 陡峭 (dǒuqiào, 'steep, precipitous').

meanings: foot of a bird or animal

components.note: 爪 depicts three curved claws or talons, like a bird's foot gripping down.

example.pinyin: Lǎoyīng de zhǎo hěn fēnglì.
example.english: The eagle's claws are very sharp.
example.fact: 爪 (zhǎo) means 'claw, talon' — in everyday speech for an animal's paw, it's often pronounced zhuǎ instead, as in 爪子 (zhuǎzi).

components.note: 兔 depicts a rabbit's body with long ears and a short tail, seen in profile.

example.pinyin: Tùzi xǐhuan chī húluóbo.
example.english: Rabbits like to eat carrots.
example.fact: 兔 means 'rabbit' and is one of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.

etymologyHint: A midwife 殳 to helping a pregnant woman 㐆; 㐆 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 㐆 depicts a person turned to one side, an early image tied to receiving care.
殳 depicts a hand holding a tool, suggesting an act of assistance — together the two parts once depicted someone caring for another, an image that broadened into 殷's meaning 'abundant, thriving.'

example.hanzi: 殷商是中国古代的一个朝代。
example.pinyin: Yīn Shāng shì Zhōngguó gǔdài de yí gè cháodài.
example.english: Yin Shang was an ancient Chinese dynasty.
example.fact: 殷 is best known as another name for the Shang dynasty (殷商, Yīn Shāng), one of China's earliest recorded dynasties.

example.pinyin: Tā hěn jiānzhēn.
example.english: He is very steadfast and loyal.
example.fact: 贞 usually appears in 坚贞 (jiānzhēn, 'steadfast, unwavering'), describing unwavering loyalty or integrity.

etymologyHint: A perennial; grass 艹 that survives 存 year-after-year

components.note: 艹 (grass) shows this is plant-related.
存 (to survive, endure) shows the grass persisting year after year — this image of something enduring and reliable extended to 荐's meaning 'to recommend.'

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī tuījiàn wǒ kàn zhè běn shū.
example.english: The teacher recommended that I read this book.
example.fact: 荐 usually appears in 推荐 (tuījiàn, 'to recommend').

meanings: sound of infant learning to talk

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哑 describes an inability to speak.
亚 (yà) gives a sound close to yǎ, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Tā kū de shēngyīn dōu yǎ le.
example.english: He cried until his voice went hoarse.
example.fact: 哑 means 'mute, hoarse,' as in 哑巴 (yǎba, 'a mute person') and 沙哑 (shāyǎ, 'hoarse').

components.note: 灰 (ash) — 炭 relates to a substance that burns down to ash, charcoal.
山 (shān) gives a sound only distantly related to tàn today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Dōngtiān wǒmen yòng mùtàn qǔnuǎn.
example.english: In winter we use charcoal to keep warm.
example.fact: 炭 usually appears in 木炭 (mùtàn, 'charcoal') and 煤炭 (méitàn, 'coal').

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坟 describes a mound of earth, a grave.
文 (wén) gives a sound only distantly related to fén today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shān shàng yǒu yí zuò fénmù.
example.english: There is a grave on the mountain.
example.fact: 坟 usually appears in 坟墓 (fénmù, 'grave, tomb').

etymologyHint: Two eyes, one open 目 and one shut 乏

components.note: 目 (eye) shows the open eye.
乏 here stands in for the other eye, closed — together depicting the quick blink of the eyes.

example.pinyin: Tā zhǎ le zhǎ yǎnjing.
example.english: She blinked her eyes.
example.fact: 眨 usually appears in 眨眼 (zhǎyǎn, 'to blink').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 搏 describes a hand-related action, fighting or striking.
尃 (fū) gives a sound only distantly related to bó today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā hé duìshǒu bódòu le hěn jiǔ.
example.english: He fought with his opponent for a long time.
example.fact: 搏 usually appears in 搏斗 (bódòu, 'to wrestle, fight') and 脉搏 (màibó, 'pulse').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咳 is a sound made with the mouth.
亥 (hài) gives a sound close to hāi, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Hāi, zhēn dǎoméi!
example.english: Ugh, what bad luck!
example.fact: 咳 has two readings: as hāi it's a sighing interjection like 'ugh,' while as ké it means 'to cough' (咳嗽, késou).

meanings: to approach; to draw near to

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拢 describes a hand-related action, gathering things together.
龙 (lóng) gives a sound close to lǒng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ tóufa lǒng dào ěr hòu.
example.english: She tucked her hair behind her ear.
example.fact: 拢 means 'to gather, bring together,' as in 靠拢 (kàolǒng, 'to draw close together').

components.note: 男 (man) — 舅 names a male relative.
臼 (jiù) gives the sound — an exact match with 舅.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiùjiu zhù zài Shànghǎi.
example.english: My uncle lives in Shanghai.
example.fact: 舅 usually appears in 舅舅 (jiùjiu, 'maternal uncle').

components.note: 日 (sun) — 昧 originally described dim, unclear light, extended to mean obscure or ignorant.
未 (wèi) gives a sound close to mèi, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Zhège xiǎngfǎ hěn yúmèi.
example.english: This idea is very ignorant and foolish.
example.fact: 昧 usually appears in 愚昧 (yúmèi, 'ignorant, unenlightened') and 暧昧 (àimèi, 'ambiguous, vague').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 擅 describes a hand-related skill, being good at something.
亶 (dǎn) gives a sound only distantly related to shàn today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā shàncháng yóuyǒng.
example.english: He is good at swimming.
example.fact: 擅 usually appears in 擅长 (shàncháng, 'to be good at, skilled in').

etymologyHint: A person 大 breathing lots of fresh air 爻

components.note: 大 depicts a person, arms and legs spread wide.
爻, shown twice around the person, suggests air or light flowing freely — together giving 爽 its meaning 'refreshing, clear.'

example.pinyin: Qiūtiān de tiānqì hěn liángshuǎng.
example.english: The autumn weather is cool and refreshing.
example.fact: 爽 usually appears in 凉爽 (liángshuǎng, 'cool and refreshing') and, in slang, means 'great, satisfying.'

meanings: (bound form) coffee; café (abbr. for 咖啡[ka1 fei1])

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咖 is used in a word for something taken by mouth (coffee).
加 (jiā) gives a sound close to kā, sharing the same rhyme with a different initial.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan hē kāfēi.
example.english: I like drinking coffee.
example.fact: 咖 only appears in 咖啡 (kāfēi, 'coffee') and 咖喱 (gālí, 'curry') — both loanwords using 咖 for its sound.

meanings: to put; to place; to leave
to put aside; to shelve; to postpone

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 搁 describes a hand-related action, placing something down.
阁 (gé) gives a sound close to gē, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Bǎ shū gē zài zhuōzi shàng.
example.english: Put the book down on the table.
example.fact: 搁 means 'to place, put down,' as in 搁置 (gēzhì, 'to shelve, put aside').

components.note: 礻 (spirit/ritual) — 禄 relates to blessings or fortune granted from above.
录 (lù) gives the sound — an exact match with 禄.

example.pinyin: Rénmen cháng shuō fúlùshòu.
example.english: People often say 'fortune, prosperity, longevity.'
example.fact: 禄 means 'good fortune, official salary' and appears in the traditional trio 福禄寿 (fú lù shòu, 'fortune, prosperity, and longevity').

components.note: 隹 (bird) — 雌 describes the female of a species, often used for animals.
此 (cǐ) gives a sound close to cí, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhī niǎo shì cí de.
example.english: This bird is female.
example.fact: 雌 means 'female' (for animals), as in 雌雄 (cíxióng, 'male and female').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哨 relates to a sound made by blowing, a whistle.
肖 (xiào) gives a sound only distantly related to shào today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī chuī shàozi jíhé dàjiā.
example.english: The teacher blew the whistle to gather everyone.
example.fact: 哨 usually appears in 哨子 (shàozi, 'whistle') and 岗哨 (gǎngshào, 'sentry post').

components.note: 凡 (all, general) — suggests broad, all-around coverage, related to 巩's meaning of making something firm throughout.
工 (gōng) gives a sound close to gǒng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 我们要巩固学过的知识。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào gǒnggù xuéguò de zhīshi.
example.english: We need to consolidate what we've learned.
example.fact: 巩 almost always appears in 巩固 (gǒnggù, 'to consolidate, strengthen').

components.note: 纟 (thread/silk) — 绢 names a type of silk fabric.
肙 (yuān) gives a sound only distantly related to juàn today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí kuài sījuàn.
example.english: This is a piece of silk fabric.
example.fact: 绢 refers to a fine silk fabric, as in 丝绢 (sījuàn, 'silk cloth').

components.note: 虫 (insect/mollusk) — 螺 names a creature, a spiral-shelled snail.
累 (lěi) gives a sound only distantly related to luó today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Hǎibiān yǒu hěn duō luó.
example.english: There are many snails by the sea.
example.fact: 螺 usually appears in 螺丝 (luósī, 'screw') and 田螺 (tiánluó, 'river snail').

components.note: 衣 (clothes) — 裹 relates to wrapping something, like fabric around an object.
果 (guǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 裹.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ lǐwù bāoguǒ hǎo le.
example.english: She wrapped the gift up.
example.fact: 裹 usually appears in 包裹 (bāoguǒ, 'package, to wrap').

etymologyHint: Twenty 廿 days ago 日

components.note: 廿 means 'twenty,' marking a span of time.
日 (day/sun) shows this is about time passing — together suggesting many days gone by, giving 昔 its meaning 'formerly, in the past.'

example.pinyin: Tā hěn xiǎngniàn xīrì de péngyou.
example.english: He misses his old friends from the past very much.
example.fact: 昔 means 'formerly, in the past,' as in 昔日 (xīrì, 'former times').

components.note: 车 (cart) — 轩 originally referred to a type of covered carriage.
干 (gān) gives a sound only distantly related to xuān today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 很多人喜欢在名字里用'轩'字。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén xǐhuan zài míngzi lǐ yòng 'xuān' zì.
example.english: Many people like to use the character 'xuān' in names.
example.fact: 轩 originally meant a covered carriage or a raised veranda; today it's mostly seen in personal names and words like 气宇轩昂 (qìyǔ xuān'áng, 'imposing and dignified').

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谬 relates to a false or mistaken statement.
翏 (liù) gives a sound only distantly related to miù today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhège shuōfǎ hěn huāngmiù.
example.english: This claim is very absurd.
example.fact: 谬 usually appears in 荒谬 (huāngmiù, 'absurd, ridiculous') and 谬论 (miùlùn, 'fallacy').

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谍 relates to secretly gathering and reporting information.
枼 (yè) gives a sound only distantly related to dié today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de jiàndié hěn cōngmíng.
example.english: The spy in the movie is very clever.
example.fact: 谍 usually appears in 间谍 (jiàndié, 'spy').

meanings: used in 龜茲|龟兹[Qiu1 ci2]

components.note: 龟 depicts a turtle seen from above, its rounded shell, head, and legs simplified into a few strokes.

example.pinyin: Wūguī zǒu de hěn màn.
example.english: Turtles walk very slowly.
example.fact: 龟 means 'turtle, tortoise' and usually appears in 乌龟 (wūguī, 'tortoise').

components.note: 女 (woman) — 媳 names a female family member.
息 (xī) gives a sound close to xí, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen jiā de xífù.
example.english: She is our family's daughter-in-law.
example.fact: 媳 usually appears in 媳妇 (xífù, 'daughter-in-law,' or colloquially, 'wife').

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 薑; grass 艹 provides the meaning while 畺 provides the pronunciation

components.note: 姜 is the simplified form of 薑, which combined a grass radical (艹, for the ginger plant) with a separate part supplying the sound; in the modern simplified shape (羊 over 女), that original plant picture has been lost.

example.pinyin: Māma yòng jiāng zuò tāng.
example.english: Mom uses ginger to make soup.
example.fact: 姜 means 'ginger' and is also a common Chinese surname.

etymologyHint: To damage 害 one's eyes 目; 害 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 目 (eye) shows this relates to sight.
害 (to harm) shows damage being done — together giving 瞎's meaning 'blind.'

example.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjing xiā le.
example.english: He went blind.
example.fact: 瞎 means 'blind' and, informally, also means 'random, reckless,' as in 瞎说 (xiāshuō, 'to talk nonsense').

example.hanzi: 他觉得很冤,因为不是他做的。
example.pinyin: Tā juéde hěn yuān, yīnwèi bú shì tā zuò de.
example.english: He feels wronged because it wasn't him who did it.
example.fact: 冤 usually appears in 冤枉 (yuānwang, 'to wrong someone unjustly') and 冤屈 (yuānqū, 'grievance, injustice').

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — 鸦 names a bird, the crow.
牙 (yá) gives a sound close to yā, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Shù shàng yǒu jǐ zhī wūyā.
example.english: There are a few crows in the tree.
example.fact: 鸦 usually appears in 乌鸦 (wūyā, 'crow').

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 蓬 names a type of plant.
逢 (féng) gives a sound close to péng, sharing the same rhyme with a different initial.

example.pinyin: Tā de tóufa hěn péngsōng.
example.english: His hair is very fluffy.
example.fact: 蓬 usually appears in 蓬松 (péngsōng, 'fluffy, puffy') and 蓬勃 (péngbó, 'vigorous, flourishing').

example.pinyin: Tā zhù zài yì tiáo xiǎo xiàng lǐ.
example.english: He lives in a small alley.
example.fact: 巷 means 'alley, lane,' a narrow street often found in older parts of Chinese cities.

components.note: 王 (jade, written as 王 in components) — 琳 describes a fine jade or gem.
林 (lín) gives the sound — an exact match with 琳.

example.pinyin: Tā de míngzi jiào Línlín.
example.english: Her name is Linlin.
example.fact: 琳 means 'fine jade' and is a common character in Chinese given names, especially for girls.

meanings: to insert; to erect (e.g. a bus stop sign)

components.note: 木 (wood/tree) — 栽 relates to planting, growing trees or plants.
戈 (gē) gives a sound only distantly related to zāi today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 爸爸在院子里栽了一棵树。
example.pinyin: Bàba zài yuànzi lǐ zāi le yì kē shù.
example.english: Dad planted a tree in the yard.
example.fact: 栽 means 'to plant,' as in 栽树 (zāi shù, 'to plant a tree').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 沾 describes getting wet or stained by a liquid.
占 (zhàn) gives a sound close to zhān, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Tā de yīfu zhān shàng le yóuqī.
example.english: His clothes got stained with paint.
example.fact: 沾 means 'to get stained with, to touch lightly,' as in 沾上 (zhānshàng, 'to get stained with').

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诈 relates to deceiving someone through words or actions.
乍 (zhà) gives the sound — an exact match with 诈.

example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn wǎngshàng de zhàpiàn!
example.english: Watch out for online scams!
example.fact: 诈 usually appears in 诈骗 (zhàpiàn, 'to defraud, scam').

meanings: to fast or abstain from meat, wine etc

components.note: 文 (culture, writing) — 斋 relates to a scholar's study or a disciplined ritual practice, both linked to culture and learning.

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zài shūzhāi lǐ dúshū.
example.english: He reads in his study every day.
example.fact: 斋 usually appears in 书斋 (shūzhāi, 'study room') and 斋饭 (zhāifàn, 'vegetarian temple food').

components.note: 目 (eye) — 瞒 relates to concealing something from someone's view.
㒼 (mán) gives the sound — an exact match with 瞒.

example.pinyin: Tā mánzhe fùmǔ qù lǚxíng le.
example.english: He went traveling without telling his parents.
example.fact: 瞒 means 'to hide the truth from someone,' as in 瞒着 (mánzhe, 'without someone's knowledge').

etymologyHint: A tiger's 虎 stripes 彡

components.note: 虎 (tiger) shows what the stripes belong to.
彡 depicts three curved lines representing stripes or markings — together giving 彪 its meaning 'tiger stripes,' extended to 'strong, robust.'

example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de hěn biāohàn.
example.english: He looks very tough and sturdy.
example.fact: 彪 usually appears in 彪悍 (biāohàn, 'sturdy and fierce') and describes something strong or vigorous.

etymologyHint: A person 㔾 being crushed under pressure 厂

components.note: 厂 (a cliff or overhang) presses down from above.
㔾 depicts a crouching person — together showing someone pinned beneath a cliff, giving 厄's meaning 'hardship, adversity.'

example.pinyin: Tā yùdào le hěn dà de èyùn.
example.english: He encountered great misfortune.
example.fact: 厄 usually appears in 厄运 (èyùn, 'misfortune, adversity').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咨 relates to speaking, asking for advice.
次 (cì) gives a sound only distantly related to zī today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ qù zīxún yīshēng.
example.english: You can go consult a doctor.
example.fact: 咨 usually appears in 咨询 (zīxún, 'to consult').

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 纺 relates to spinning thread.
方 (fāng) gives a sound close to fǎng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng zhǔyào fǎngshā.
example.english: This factory mainly spins yarn.
example.fact: 纺 usually appears in 纺纱 (fǎngshā, 'to spin yarn') and 纺织 (fǎngzhī, 'textile, weaving').

components.note: 缶 (jar/pottery) — 罐 names a type of container, a jar or pot.
雚 (guàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 罐.

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yí gè chá guàn.
example.english: There is a tea jar on the table.
example.fact: 罐 usually appears in 罐头 (guàntou, 'canned food') and 易拉罐 (yìlāguàn, 'aluminum can').

components.note: 木 (wood) — 桶 names an object often made of wood, a bucket.
甬 (yǒng) gives a sound only distantly related to tǒng today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā tí zhe yí gè shuǐtǒng.
example.english: He is carrying a bucket of water.
example.fact: 桶 usually appears in 水桶 (shuǐtǒng, 'water bucket') and 垃圾桶 (lājītǒng, 'trash can').

components.note: 土 (earth) — 壤 names a type of earth, soil.
襄 (xiāng) gives a sound only distantly related to rǎng today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de tǔrǎng hěn féiwò.
example.english: The soil here is very fertile.
example.fact: 壤 usually appears in 土壤 (tǔrǎng, 'soil').

components.note: 米 (rice) — 糕 names a food made from rice or flour, a cake.
羔 (gāo) gives the sound — an exact match with 糕.

example.hanzi: 妈妈做了一个生日蛋糕。
example.pinyin: Māma zuò le yí gè shēngrì dàngāo.
example.english: Mom made a birthday cake.
example.fact: 糕 usually appears in 蛋糕 (dàngāo, 'cake') and 年糕 (niángāo, 'New Year rice cake').

components.note: 页 (page/head) — 颂 relates to formally praising someone, historically recorded in writing.
公 (gōng) gives a sound only distantly related to sòng today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Dàjiā yìqǐ gēsòng zǔguó.
example.english: Everyone sings in praise of the motherland together.
example.fact: 颂 usually appears in 歌颂 (gēsòng, 'to sing the praises of, extol').

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 膨 describes a body or object swelling in size.
彭 (péng) gives the sound — an exact match with 膨.

example.pinyin: Qìqiú péngzhàng qǐlái le.
example.english: The balloon expanded and inflated.
example.fact: 膨 usually appears in 膨胀 (péngzhàng, 'to expand, swell').

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谐 relates to getting along well, through agreeable speech or action.
皆 (jiē) gives a sound only distantly related to xié today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 大家希望社会更加和谐。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā xīwàng shèhuì gèngjiā héxié.
example.english: Everyone hopes society will be more harmonious.
example.fact: 谐 usually appears in 和谐 (héxié, 'harmonious') and 诙谐 (huīxié, 'witty, humorous').

meanings: to build with stones, bricks etc

components.note: 土 (earth) — 垒 describes piling up earth or stones.
厽 (lěi) gives the sound — an exact match with 垒.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在沙滩上垒城堡。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài shātān shàng lěi chéngbǎo.
example.english: The kids are building a castle on the beach by stacking sand.
example.fact: 垒 means 'to pile up, build by stacking,' and in baseball also means 'base,' as in 一垒 (yī lěi, 'first base').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咕 is an onomatopoeic sound made with the mouth.
古 (gǔ) gives a sound close to gū, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Tā de dùzi gūgū jiào.
example.english: His stomach is rumbling.
example.fact: 咕 is an onomatopoeic character, as in 咕咕 (gūgū), the sound of a rumbling stomach or a cooing pigeon.

etymologyHint: A crack 日 dividing two things 小; 阝 provides the pronunciation

components.note: 日 depicts a narrow gap or shaft of light.
小, appearing twice, shows two separate small things — together with 日 evoking a sliver of light passing through a crack, giving 隙 its meaning 'gap, crack.'

example.pinyin: Ménfèng lǐ yǒu yí dào fèngxì.
example.english: There is a crack in the doorway.
example.fact: 隙 usually appears in 缝隙 (fèngxì, 'crack, gap') and 空隙 (kòngxì, 'gap, space').

components.note: 辛 (bitter/pungent) — 辣 describes a pungent, spicy taste.
束 (shù) gives a sound only distantly related to là today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Sìchuān cài hěn là.
example.english: Sichuan food is very spicy.
example.fact: 辣 means 'spicy, hot,' and is central to describing Sichuan and Hunan cuisine.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 绑 relates to tying something with thread or rope.
邦 (bāng) gives a sound close to bǎng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ xiédài bǎng hǎo le.
example.english: He tied his shoelaces.
example.fact: 绑 means 'to tie, bind,' as in 绑鞋带 (bǎng xiédài, 'to tie shoelaces').

components.note: 宀 (roof/shelter) — 宠 relates to being kept and favored within a household.
龙 (lóng) gives a sound only distantly related to chǒng today, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā hěn chǒng'ài tā de nǚ'ér.
example.english: He dotes on his daughter a lot.
example.fact: 宠 usually appears in 宠爱 (chǒng'ài, 'to dote on') and 宠物 (chǒngwù, 'pet').

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嘿 is a sound made with the mouth, an interjection.
黑 (hēi) gives the sound — an exact match with 嘿.

example.pinyin: Hēi, nǐ zài zuò shénme?
example.english: Hey, what are you doing?
example.fact: 嘿 is an interjection used to get someone's attention, similar to 'hey' in English.

etymologyHint: A beast 兄 with two horns 丷

components.note: 丷 depicts two small horns.
兄 here forms the body of a creature — together an early image of a horned animal; the character later shifted to mean 'to exchange, convert.'

example.hanzi: 我想把美元兑换成人民币。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ Měiyuán duìhuàn chéng Rénmínbì.
example.english: I want to exchange dollars for RMB.
example.fact: 兑 usually appears in 兑换 (duìhuàn, 'to exchange currency').

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 霉 relates to dampness, the condition that lets mold grow.
每 (měi) gives a sound close to méi, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Miànbāo fàng jiǔ le huì zhǎng méi.
example.english: If bread sits too long, it will grow mold.
example.fact: 霉 usually appears in 发霉 (fāméi, 'to go moldy') and, in slang, 倒霉 (dǎoméi, 'to have bad luck').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 挫 describes a hand-related action, pushing down or grinding.
坐 (zuò) gives a sound close to cuò, sharing the same rhyme with a different initial.

example.pinyin: Tā yùdào le hěn dà de cuòzhé.
example.english: He encountered a major setback.
example.fact: 挫 usually appears in 挫折 (cuòzhé, 'setback, frustration').

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 稽 was originally tied to inspecting or delaying, later meaning to examine.
旨 (zhǐ) gives a sound only distantly related to jī today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他获得了大学的稽核证书。
example.pinyin: Tā huòdé le dàxué de jīhé zhèngshū.
example.english: He obtained a university auditing certificate.
example.fact: 稽 usually appears in 稽核 (jīhé, 'to audit, examine') and 滑稽 (huájī, 'funny, comical').

components.note: 车 (cart/wheel) — 辐 relates to parts of a wheel, the spokes.
畐 (fú) gives the sound — an exact match with 辐.

example.hanzi: 自行车的轮子有很多辐条。
example.pinyin: Zìxíngchē de lúnzi yǒu hěn duō fútiáo.
example.english: A bicycle wheel has many spokes.
example.fact: 辐 usually appears in 辐条 (fútiáo, 'spoke of a wheel') and 辐射 (fúshè, 'radiation'), both describing lines spreading out from a center.
